en: The Theravāda Vinaya:
The Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga,
Chapter on Forfeiture (Nissaggiyakaṇḍa)
The Second Chapter on the Set of Rules: The Training Rule on Receiving Out-of-Season Robe-Cloth.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

Now at that time, a number of bhikkhunīs who had completed the rains residence in a village monastery went to Sāvatthī; they were perfect in their conduct, perfect in their deportment, poorly clad, and wearing coarse robes.

When the lay followers saw those bhikkhunīs, thinking, "These bhikkhunīs are perfect in their conduct, perfect in their deportment, poorly clad, and wearing coarse robes; these bhikkhunīs must have been robbed," they gave an out-of-season robe to the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs.
The bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having determined, "Our kaṭhina has been spread; this is cloth for the proper season," had it distributed.
When the lay followers saw those bhikkhunīs, they said this:
“Have you received a robe?
“We have not received a robe, friend.
The lady Thullanandā—”
“Having determined, ‘Our *kaṭhina* has been spread; this is a timely robe-cloth,’ she had it distributed.
The lay followers complained, grumbled, and voiced their indignation:
“How can the noble lady Thullanandā determine that an untimely robe-cloth is a ‘timely robe-cloth’ and then have it distributed?”
The bhikkhunīs heard those lay followers complaining, criticizing, and grumbling.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [as above]... complained, criticized, and grumbled:
"How can the noble lady Thullanandā determine an out-of-season robe to be 'in-season' and then have it distributed?"
Then those bhikkhunīs reported this matter to the bhikkhus.
The bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One.
… [as before] … “Is it true, bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having determined an out-of-season robe to be ‘an in-season robe,’ had it distributed?”

“It is true, Blessed One. The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them: “… How indeed, monks, can the nun Thullanandā, having determined an out-of-season robe to be ‘a robe for the proper season,’ cause it to be distributed? This is not suitable, monks, for the training of those who have gone forth. Thus the Blessed One spoke. Having rebuked them and given a Dhamma talk, he addressed the monks: “Monks, this rule of training should be laid down thus: ‘If a nun, having determined an out-of-season robe to be a robe for the proper season, should cause it to be distributed, there is an offense of wrong-doing. [The Blessed One further addressed the monks: “And how, monks, is it an out-of-season robe? It is one that has not been received during the robe season; this is called an out-of-season robe. And how, monks, is it a robe for the proper season? It is one that has been received during the robe season; this is called a robe for the proper season. “Monks, there are these five kinds of robes for the proper season: the robe received at the beginning of the robe season, the robe received at the middle of the robe season, the robe received at the end of the robe season, the robe received after the robe season has ended, and the robe received when the robe season is extended. These, monks, are the five kinds of robes for the proper season. “Monks, there are these five kinds of out-of-season robes: the robe received before the robe season has begun, the robe received while the robe season is still unextended, the robe received after the robe season has ended, the robe received when the robe season is no longer being extended, and the robe received when the robe season has been cut off. These, monks, are the five kinds of out-of-season robes. “If a nun, having determined an out-of-season robe to be a robe for the proper season, should cause it to be distributed, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she distributes it thinking it is an out-of-season robe, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she is in doubt as to whether it is an out-of-season robe, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she distributes it thinking it is a robe for the proper season, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she distributes it thinking it is an out-of-season robe when it is actually a robe for the proper season, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she is in doubt as to whether it is a robe for the proper season, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she distributes it thinking it is an out-of-season robe when it is actually an out-of-season robe, there is an offense of wrong-doing. If she is in doubt as to whether it is an out-of-season robe, there is an offense of wrong-doing. “There is no offense if she determines it to be an out-of-season robe and distributes it as such; if she determines it to be a robe for the proper season and distributes it as such; if she is insane; if she is deranged; if she is afflicted by pain; if she is the first offender.”
“Monks, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And thus, monks, should the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule:
‘If any bhikkhunī, having determined an out-of-season robe to be an in-season robe, should have it distributed, it is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession (nissaggiya-pācittiya).’”
"But whichever" means whichever such... "nun" means...
[as before]... nun.
... [as before] ... this is what is intended by the term "bhikkhunī" in this context.
"Out-of-season robe-cloth" (akālacīvara) means:

that which arises during the eleven months when the Kathina has not been spread; that which arises during the seven months when the Kathina has been spread; and that which is given specifically designated even during the proper season—this is called out-of-season robe-cloth.
If one resolves that an out-of-season robe-cloth is a "seasonal robe-cloth" and causes it to be distributed, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*) for the act of proposing;
upon acquisition, it becomes subject to relinquishment (*nissaggiya*).
It must be relinquished to the Saṅgha, to a group, or to a single bhikkhunī.
And furthermore, monks, it should be relinquished in this way:
“… ‘Venerable ladies, this out-of-season robe-cloth which I determined to be ‘seasonal robe-cloth’ and had distributed is to be relinquished; I relinquish it to the Saṅgha. …pe…
“...should give,” ...
“they should give,” ...
“I give to the noble lady.”

If it is out-of-season robe-cloth and she perceives it as such, yet having determined it to be "in-season robe-cloth," she causes it to be distributed, there is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession (nissaggiya-pācittiya).
If it is out-of-season robe-cloth and she is doubtful, yet having determined it to be "in-season robe-cloth," she causes it to be distributed, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If it is out-of-season robe-cloth and she perceives it as in-season robe-cloth, yet having determined it to be "in-season robe-cloth," she causes it to be distributed, there is no offense.
If it is a timely robe, but she perceives it as an untimely robe, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If it is a timely robe, but she is uncertain of it, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is a timely robe, and she perceives it as a timely robe, there is no offense.
There is no offense if one causes [the robe] to be distributed while perceiving it as an out-of-season robe when it is an out-of-season robe,
or if one causes [the robe] to be distributed while perceiving it as an in-season robe when it is an in-season robe.
"In the case of one who is insane,
or in the case of one who is a first-offender.
The second training rule is finished.
